# Generation Conventions

Rules every generated automation must follow. Generator agents read this file before writing code.

## The autogenerated marker (mandatory)

Every generated file carries **both** markers so manually written and generated automations stay distinguishable:

1. **Banner comment** — the very first thing in the file, before imports:

```js
/**
 * AUTO-GENERATED automation — created by the spell-automation-generate skill
 * from <report file> (<generation date>).
 * Proposal feasibility: <ready | needs-new-event (...) | needs-gm-or-rights (...)>.
 * Degraded parts (manual): <list, or "none">.
 *
 * Review before trusting. Regenerating this spell OVERWRITES this file.
 * To adopt as manually maintained: remove this banner and the `autogenerated`
 * flag in the definition below — regeneration will then refuse to touch it.
 */
```

2. **`autogenerated: true`** field in the exported definition object, right after `version`. The registry ignores unknown fields, so this is inert at runtime but machine-readable:

```js
export const rayOfFrost = {
    id: 'rayOfFrost',
    name: 'Ray of Frost',
    description: '...',
    version: '1.0.0',
    autogenerated: true,
    ...
};
```

To list all autogenerated automations later: `grep -rl "autogenerated: true" scripts/automations`.

## Overwrite policy

Before generating a spell whose target folder already exists, read the existing file's first lines:

- Banner present (`AUTO-GENERATED automation`) → regeneration may overwrite it.
- No banner → the file is manually created or adopted. **Never overwrite.** Skip the spell and report it as `skipped-manual`.

## File layout and naming

One folder per automation, matching the existing tree:

```
scripts/automations/<kebab-case-name>/<camelCaseId>.js
```

- `id` / export name: camelCase of the spell name with apostrophes stripped (`Drayfn's Bane of Excellence` → `drayfnsBaneOfExcellence`).
- Folder: kebab-case (`drayfns-bane-of-excellence`).
- The parse script computes these; use its values verbatim.
- Agents create **only** their own folder and file. Never touch `_index.js`, framework files, other automations, `module.json`, or `lang/` — the orchestrator wires registration afterwards.

## Definition checklist

Follow the documented shape in `scripts/framework/registry.js` (the docblock at the top is the contract). Required/expected fields:

- `id`, `name` (the spell's English name), `version: '1.0.0'`, `autogenerated: true`.
- `description` — one to three sentences for the manager UI: what is automated **and what is intentionally left manual**. This is where degraded parts must be visible to the user.
- `match.itemNames: ['<Spell Name>']` — contains-matching, case-insensitive. If the proposal targets one rules version only (e.g. PHB'24), still match the plain name; note the version caveat in `description`.
- `settings` — map the proposal's "Settings" line to per-item settings fields (`checkbox`/`select`/`number`/`text`). Every degradable behavior should get an `auto-apply vs. off`-style toggle when the proposal calls for one (never a "chat reminder" mode — see "Degrade to effects"). Omit the array if the proposal says "none".
- `events` — only events that exist in `scripts/framework/triggers.js`. Do not invent event names.
- `init` — only when a native Foundry hook is genuinely needed (e.g. `deleteActiveEffect` cleanup, as in Shadow Blade).

## Available events (verify against triggers.js at generation time)

- `spellCastConfigure` — before the usage dialog; synchronous; may mutate usage/dialog config.
- `spellCastComplete` — after a spell activity is used (hit or miss, before attack/damage rolls); has `castLevel`, `results`, `message`.
- `damageRollConfigure` — synchronous, before the damage roll dialog/evaluation, on the rolling client; may mutate `config.rolls` (an array of `{data, parts, options}` roll configurations — push parts, add `options.types`, append whole roll entries). Crit doubling is applied natively afterwards. Never cancel the roll.
- `damageRollComplete` — after a damage chat card is created; has `damageRolls`, `damageTotal`, `setDamageRolls(rolls)` to rewrite the card. The original rolls are already evaluated (and animated) when this fires — to change WHAT is rolled, prefer `damageRollConfigure` (see "Prefer *Configure rewrites" below).
- `featureUseComplete` — feat items, rarely relevant for spells.
- `attackRollConfigure` — synchronous, before the attack roll dialog/evaluation, on the attacking client; may push parts into `config.rolls[0].parts` ('-1d4'), set `options.advantage`/`options.disadvantage`, or lower `options.criticalSuccess` (crit threshold). Has `targets` (the attacker's targets with `actor`/`ac`).
- `attackRollComplete` — after the attack roll evaluates, on the attacking client; has `roll`, `isCritical`, `isFumble`, `d20`, and `targets` each with `hit` (true/false when AC known, crits hit, fumbles miss, else undefined) plus `hitTargets`.
- `saveRollConfigure` — synchronous, before a saving throw dialog/evaluation, **on the client rolling the save** — that client owns the rolling actor, so marker effects on it can be read and (in the complete event) deleted. May mutate parts/advantage. Includes concentration saves.
- `saveRollComplete` — after a saving throw, on the rolling client; has `roll`, `ability`, `total`, `dc`, `isSuccess`, `isFailure`, `margin`, `d20` (dc-derived fields are `undefined` when the save was rolled without a DC, e.g. from the sheet instead of the spell card's save button).

**Effect-scope routing:** attack/save events match automations not just by item/actor name but by module-flagged active effects on any involved actor (the roller, or an attack target). Flag every marker effect you create with `flags: {[MODULE_ID]: {<automationId>: true}}` (any truthy value or a data object) — the marked actor's later attack/save rolls then route to your handlers, where you can consume the marker. Store per-marker data (origin spell uuid, charges, damage type) inside that flag object.

Movement/turn events, region-enter events, and damage-taken events still **do not exist** — those parts must degrade (see below).

## Cross-client writes (GM relay)

The framework provides sanctioned helpers in `scripts/framework/utils.js` for writing to actors the acting user does not own:

- `applyEffectToActor(actor, effectData)` — creates the effect directly when owned, otherwise relays to the active GM's client. Returns `'applied'`, `'relayed'`, or `false` (no ownership AND no GM online). The effect data **must** carry a `flags[MODULE_ID]` entry or the relay refuses it.
- `deleteDocument(doc)` — same contract for deleting module-flagged documents (marker cleanup).

Always branch on the return value: on `false`, skip the write and `console.warn` it with the module prefix (never post a chat card). Never call `game.socket` or register socket handlers directly in generated code — the helpers are the only sanctioned cross-client path.

Remember: `saveRollConfigure`/`saveRollComplete` handlers already run on the client that OWNS the rolling actor — applying or consuming effects on the save roller there is a plain owned write, no relay needed.

## Degradation rules

The hard rule (module policy): **never block, cancel, or delay the player's vanilla cast or roll.** Automations layer on top; when a capability is missing at runtime, degrade to an applied marker effect or, failing that, to nothing.

Per feasibility:

- **ready** — implement fully. Still guard edge cases (no target selected, roll structure unparseable) by leaving the vanilla roll untouched instead of throwing.
- **needs-new-event** — implement every part the existing events support (cast-time dialogs, damage-card rewrites, attack/save roll events, effects on the caster's own actor/items). The parts needing a still-missing event (movement/turn, region-enter, damage-taken) become a marker effect whose description carries the computed manual rule.
- **needs-gm-or-rights** — write to non-owned actors only through `applyEffectToActor`/`deleteDocument` (see "Cross-client writes" above); when they return `false`, skip the write and `console.warn` it with the module prefix. Never raw sockets in generated code.

List every degraded part in the banner and summarize it in `description`.

## Degrade to effects — NEVER chat reminders

**Generated code must never post chat reminder/note cards** (user decision 2026-07-07: they are table noise and were all removed from the module). Do not emit a `postReminder`/`postNote` helper, `fantik-automations reminder` chat cards, or "reminder-only" settings modes. Degradation order:

1. **Applied marker effect** — whenever the missing piece is "detect X later and resolve it", put a visible ActiveEffect on the affected actor via `applyEffectToActor` (name it after the rider, e.g. "Booming Energy", flag it for effect-scope routing, stamp the COMPUTED numbers for this cast — dice already scaled to the caster's level — into the effect description). The GM adjudicates off the marker; nothing needs re-reading or re-computing at the table.
2. **Nothing** — when no actor can carry a marker (no target, `applyEffectToActor` returned false), leave the vanilla cast/roll untouched and `console.warn` the skipped write with the module prefix. Roll rewrites already show their result in the card's formula; no explanatory chat card is wanted.

## Code style

Match the existing automations (`shadow-blade/shadowBlade.js`, `gamblers-blade/gamblersBlade.js`, `bladesong/bladesong.js`, `darkness/darkness.js`):

- ES module; import `MODULE_ID` from `../../framework/constants.js` and helpers from `../../framework/utils.js` as needed.
- 4-space indentation, single quotes, semicolons.
- A JSDoc block after the banner describing behavior, per-item settings, and what is not automated — same register as Shadow Blade's header comment.
- Handlers are small named `async function`s; comments state constraints ("only the acting client runs this"), not narration.
- Reuse framework utilities before writing new helpers; put spell-specific helpers in the automation's own file.

## Weapon picker pattern (True Strike, Booming Blade, Green-Flame Blade, …)

Any automation that asks the player which weapon they strike with **must** copy the picker from `true-strike/trueStrike.js` / `booming-blade/boomingBlade.js`. Three behavioral rules are non-negotiable (earlier generations got them wrong):

1. **Never hide weapons.** Players routinely don't maintain the equipped state in their inventory, so filtering to equipped-only strands them with an empty or wrong list. The `weaponFilter` setting only **orders** the list — `'equipped'` sorts equipped weapons first, everything is always listed:

```js
/**
 * Candidate weapons the player may strike with. Never hides any — players
 * routinely don't maintain the equipped state in their inventory, so the
 * 'equipped' filter only ORDERS the list (equipped first, the likely picks).
 */
function pickableWeapons(actor, filter) {
    const weapons = actor.items.filter(item => item.type === 'weapon');
    if (filter === 'equipped') {
        weapons.sort((a, b) => (b.system?.equipped ? 1 : 0) - (a.system?.equipped ? 1 : 0));
    }
    return weapons;
}
```

2. **The dialog is a dropdown, not a button row.** A button per weapon caps the list (the old pattern cut off at 8) and overflows for hoarders; a `<select>` fits an arsenal of any size. Unequipped weapons get a `(not equipped)` suffix so equipped-first ordering stays legible. The dialog also carries an **"Always use this weapon (don't ask again)" checkbox** and returns `{weapon, remember}` (or `null` on cancel):

```js
/**
 * Weapon picker dialog — a dropdown, so an arsenal of any size fits (button rows
 * capped the list). Returns {weapon, remember} or null on cancel; remember is the
 * "don't ask again" checkbox, persisted by the caller into the per-item settings.
 */
async function chooseWeapon(spell, weapons) {
    const options = weapons.map((weapon, index) => {
        const suffix = weapon.system?.equipped ? '' : ' (not equipped)';
        return `<option value="${weapon.id}"${index === 0 ? ' selected' : ''}>${weapon.name}${suffix}</option>`;
    }).join('');
    const result = await foundry.applications.api.DialogV2.wait({
        window: {title: `${spell.name}: choose a weapon`},
        content: '<p>Which weapon are you striking with?</p>'
            + `<select name="weapon" autofocus style="width: 100%">${options}</select>`
            + '<label style="display: flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; margin-top: 8px;">'
            + '<input type="checkbox" name="remember"> Always use this weapon (don\'t ask again)</label>',
        buttons: [
            {
                action: 'strike',
                label: 'Strike',
                default: true,
                callback: (event, button) => ({
                    id: button.form?.elements.weapon?.value ?? null,
                    remember: button.form?.elements.remember?.checked ?? false
                })
            },
            {action: 'cancel', label: 'Cancel', icon: 'fa-solid fa-xmark'}
        ],
        rejectClose: false
    });
    if (!result || result === 'cancel' || !result.id) return null;
    const weapon = weapons.find(w => w.id === result.id) ?? null;
    return weapon ? {weapon, remember: result.remember} : null;
}
```

3. **Preselection skips the picker.** A per-item text setting `defaultWeapon` (default `''`) names a weapon to always use; when a weapon with that exact name exists, the dialog never opens. When the weapon is gone (dropped/renamed), fall back to asking — never block. Ticking the checkbox persists the chosen weapon's **name** into that same setting via `setFlag`, so it shows up (and is clearable) in Manage Automations. Selection flow in the cast handler:

```js
// A preselected weapon (the setting, filled by hand or by the picker's
// "don't ask again" checkbox) skips the dialog entirely; if it is gone
// (dropped/renamed), fall back to asking.
const preset = (context.settings?.defaultWeapon ?? '').trim();
let weapon = preset ? weapons.find(w => w.name === preset) ?? null : null;
if (!weapon && weapons.length === 1) weapon = weapons[0];
if (!weapon) {
    const choice = await chooseWeapon(context.item, weapons);
    weapon = choice?.weapon ?? null;
    if (weapon && choice.remember) {
        // Persist into the per-item settings so Manage Automations shows the
        // name (clear the field there to be asked again). Written to the
        // actor's canonical spell — context.item may be an ephemeral clone.
        const spell = actor.items.get(context.item.id) ?? context.item;
        await spell.setFlag(MODULE_ID, 'settings.<automationId>.defaultWeapon', weapon.name).catch(() => {});
    }
}
if (!weapon) return; // player cancelled the picker — the vanilla cast already happened
```

Surrounding conventions that go with the picker:

- **Skip the dialog when there is exactly one weapon** (the `weapons.length === 1` branch above).
- **Empty list never blocks the cast** — return without touching the spell's own rolls (no chat card).
- **Cancel never blocks either** — the vanilla cast already happened; return, and clear any flag/snapshot set earlier in the handler so stale weapon data can't leak into the next roll (see the `unsetFlag` on cancel in `boomingBlade.js`).
- **The `weaponFilter` setting** is a select named "Weapon order" whose hint states that every weapon is always listed, with choices `equipped: 'Equipped weapons first'` and `all: 'Inventory order'`, default `'equipped'`.
- **The `defaultWeapon` setting** is a text field named "Preselected weapon", default `''`, with the hint: `'Exact name of the weapon to always strike with — the picker is skipped while this is set. Filled by the picker\'s "don\'t ask again" checkbox; clear it to be asked again. If no weapon by this name is found, the picker opens.'`

## Prefer *Configure rewrites over *Complete card surgery

When a roll needs changing, rewrite it in the `*Configure` event (`damageRollConfigure` / `attackRollConfigure`), not by patching the chat card afterwards in the `*Complete` event. Configure-time parts appear in the roll dialog, are rolled and animated once, and get native crit doubling; post-hoc `setDamageRolls` surgery evaluates and animates extra rolls after the fact and has to fake all of that. Reserve `*Complete` handlers for reading results and cleanup — see `true-strike/trueStrike.js` (v1.3.0): `configureStrike` does every rewrite, `applyStrike` only clears the pending flag.

**Damage-type choices must NOT use a custom pre-cast dialog.** To offer a type conversion (e.g. True Strike's weapon-or-radiant), give the base damage part multiple types in `damageRollConfigure` — dnd5e's damage dialog then renders its **native type selector**, and picking the alternative genuinely converts the dice's type (no reminder, no card surgery):

```js
function configureStrike(context) {
    const weapon = context.item;
    const pending = weapon?.getFlag?.(MODULE_ID, 'trueStrike');
    if (!pending) return;
    const rolls = context.config?.rolls;
    if (!rolls?.length) return;

    // Base part offers radiant alongside the weapon's own type — the damage
    // dialog shows dnd5e's native type selector.
    const first = rolls[0];
    first.options ??= {};
    const types = new Set(first.options.types ?? []);
    if (first.options.type) types.add(first.options.type);
    types.add(pending.weaponType);
    types.add('radiant');
    first.options.types = [...types];

    // Flat corrections fold into the base part...
    const delta = abilityMod(context.actor, pending.spellAbility) - weaponAbilityMod(weapon, context.actor);
    if (delta !== 0) {
        first.parts ??= [];
        first.parts.push(String(delta));
    }

    // ...and bonus dice join as their own part — shown in the dialog, rolled and
    // animated once, crit-doubled natively.
    if (pending.dice > 0) {
        rolls.push({
            data: first.data ?? {},
            parts: [`${pending.dice}d6`],
            options: {type: 'radiant', types: ['radiant']}
        });
    }
}
```

Handlers for `*Configure` events must stay synchronous (dnd5e does not await the hook) — no dialogs, no `await`. Anything needing player input happens earlier (cast time) and travels via a flag, as above.

## Proven patterns to copy

- **Roll rewrite at configure time** — mutate `config.rolls` in `damageRollConfigure`/`attackRollConfigure`; see "Prefer *Configure rewrites" above (`trueStrike.js`).
- **Damage-card rewrite (last resort)** — only when the data needed does not exist until after the roll: build new `CONFIG.Dice.DamageRoll` rolls, call `context.setDamageRolls`, show Dice So Nice if active (`gamblersBlade.js`).
- **Temporary item lifecycle** — create an owned item on cast, bind it to the concentration effect's uuid, delete via `deleteActiveEffect` hook + `firstActiveOwner(...)?.isSelf` election (`shadowBlade.js`).
- **Cast-time choice** — prompt with a dialog in `spellCastComplete` (or mutate configs synchronously in `spellCastConfigure`), store the choice in scope or on a flag.
- **Weapon picker** — see "Weapon picker pattern" above; copy it verbatim, never reinvent it with a filtered list or button-row dialog.
- **Self-buff / effect on own actor** — `actor.createEmbeddedDocuments('ActiveEffect', ...)` is safe: the caster owns their own actor.
- **Reading other actors** — reading a target's HP, conditions, or type is always safe (replicated data); only **writes** need ownership.
